reason: Punching the disc seems like a direct way to make the star shapes.
expectation: I expect a disc with star-shaped holes that can eventually cast points of light, though the exact pattern is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The lamp needs power too, but I want to prepare the stars first.

effect: The punched star disc is ready; it can now be fitted to the spindle.
reaction: A straightforward start, though the result gives no detail about the holes.
reason: The spindle should let the star disc turn, which seems useful for making moving stars.
expectation: I expect the star disc to be mounted on the spindle, ready to turn inside the box.

alternatives.reason: The lamp will need power, but I want to finish preparing the disc first.

effect: The star disc and spindle have become a shadow wheel; I can now prepare the box or lamp power.
reaction: The name makes its role clearer, though I haven't seen it turn yet.
reason: The lamp needs a switched power supply to illuminate the star disc.
expectation: I expect a battery-powered switched lead ready to connect to the lamp.

alternatives.reason: The reflective lining also prepares the theatre, but I want to assemble the power supply first.

effect: The switched lamp supply is ready; the box lining is the only offered gameplay action.
reaction: Straightforward preparation, without seeing the lighting effect yet.
reason: I'm following the only available combination to prepare the theatre box.
expectation: I expect the lining to be fitted inside the box, probably reflecting light from the lamp.

effect: The box is lined and ready for the lamp.
reaction: Straightforward preparation; I am curious to see the light and shadows.
reason: Fitting the lamp is the only offered gameplay action and should prepare the light source.
expectation: I expect the LED lamp to be installed in the box, ready to connect to the switched supply.

effect: The lamp is installed, and its switched supply can now be connected.
reaction: Another straightforward assembly step; the light effect is still to come.
reason: Connecting the supply is the only offered gameplay action and should power the lamp.
expectation: I expect the lamp to have switched battery power, ready to illuminate the shadow wheel.

effect: The theatre now has power and is ready for the shadow wheel.
reaction: The assembly is progressing predictably; I still want to see the stars.
reason: The shadow wheel is the only offered gameplay action and should put the star pattern in the light's path.
expectation: I expect the wheel to be fitted inside the powered theatre, ready to cast moving star patterns, though it may still need a screen.

effect: The star wheel is fitted; the screen is the remaining offered assembly step.
reaction: The setup is nearly complete, but I haven't seen its shadows yet.
reason: The screen is the only offered gameplay action and should give the stars a surface to appear on.
expectation: I expect the tracing paper to show a star pattern, possibly moving when the wheel turns.

effect: The theatre produces moving light, but the star shapes appear as blurry blobs; the chapter ends before I learn how to sharpen them.
reaction: The moving blobs are an intriguing result and a welcome surprise after the predictable assembly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the screen was most worthwhile because it finally showed what the assembled theatre could do, including the unexpected blurry result.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence of lining, lamp, and power fittings felt repetitive: each was the only offered gameplay action and gave little feedback beyond a new item name.

surprise.text: I expected a star pattern, so seeing pale blobs instead changed my understanding of the result.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, but several required fittings were predictable and offered little meaningful choice.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to find out why the stars are blurry and whether the theatre can make them sharper; this chapter raised that question without resolving it.
